query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to produce the improvement, a measurable outcome relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with clear observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Improving hardness and strength of high-entropy alloys without sacrificing mechanical performance can be achieved through grain refinement via severe plastic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in their as-cast state.
generation.mechanism: Dislocation density increase and grain boundary strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and strength without significant loss in ductility
generation.boundary: Applicable to high-entropy alloys with face-centered cubic crystal structure
generation.uncertainty: Effect of severe plastic deformation on other mechanical properties such as fatigue resistance
generation.falsification_experiment: Compare the mechanical properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys with those of as-cast alloys. If no improvement in hardness and strength is observed, the hypothesis is falsified.
